break_rulings.why: The change makes the KV Cache gauge show real usage on all platforms and adds CPU usage on macOS; these are fixes, not breaks.
Generated image filenames now include call.id for uniqueness, but this is an additive change that does not break any documented contract.
llamacpp:cuda now reports unsupported when the NVIDIA driver is missing or too old; this catches a previously silent failure and improves user experience by falling through to Vulkan.
The /system-info API gains five new optional backend metadata fields; existing consumers simply see additional data and are not broken.
The Monitor panel gains optional new fields for multi-GPU data; this is additive to the existing schema and does not break consumers.
Image IDs and direct analysis are new features with additive fields that are never persisted; existing conversations are unaffected.

breaks: Requests that previously succeeded without authentication on API and metrics routes now return 401 when LEMONADE_API_KEY is set and LEMONADE_ADMIN_API_KEY is explicitly empty.
break_rulings.why: This tightens authentication on a misconfiguration that previously allowed empty-key bypass; only setups with a non-empty API key and an explicitly empty admin key are affected.
This is a CI workflow change only; no user-facing API, CLI, config, or artifact is altered.
The /api/chat and /api/generate endpoints now return 400 instead of 500 for non-LLM models; 500 was incorrect for client errors, so this fixes the status code rather than breaking working setups.
Alias resolution on /api/show is a bug fix returning 200 instead of 404; /api/pull and /api/delete now correctly refuse aliases named :latest instead of silently acting on the target.

breaks: Upgrading the TheNoise shared backend from v0.12.1 to v0.15.0 may change inference behavior, sampler handling, or memory layout for existing models shipped with the release.
break_rulings.why: A major version jump in the shared backend binary can alter behavior for models that were working under the previous version, and users will silently receive the new binary on upgrade.
The /pull/variants endpoint now returns 400 instead of 500 for unsupported repositories; 500 was the wrong code for a client error, so this corrects the status rather than breaking working setups.

evidence.blockers: The empty LEMONADE_ADMIN_API_KEY authentication bypass (5440e3e) was merged without manual release testing and must be verified before shipping. The NVIDIA driver gating (d4f53e7) must be confirmed on real hardware to ensure CUDA users are not unexpectedly routed to Vulkan. The ctx_size=0 router crash (13ed8c9-2) is a known bug that ships unpatched. The TheNoise backend upgrade (0c2aa03-4) needs regression testing against existing models.
evidence.breaking_changes: The only breaking change this release ships is the TheNoise shared backend upgrade from v0.12.1 to v0.15.0, which may alter inference behavior for existing models. The authentication fix tightens behavior only for misconfigured installations with LEMONADE_API_KEY set and LEMONADE_ADMIN_API_KEY explicitly empty; working setups are unaffected.
evidence.coverage: 48 commits reviewed across the full range from v2026.46.2 to 4d0568a. All 48 CI workflows passed for their respective PRs. ROCm hardware paths (gfx1170/gfx1171) and the audio transcription path were tested locally only and not exercised by CI or a human on a release candidate build.
evidence.manual_testing: GUI features need end-to-end exercise: multi-GPU monitor selection (d053087), image download/copy buttons (835eb91), image analysis/editing workflows (d58fd33), custom model registration for TheNoise and SD.cpp (2608f07), and multi-shard file listing (322675a). ROCm gfx117x hardware paths need real GPU verification (fe43f6f). The audio transcription path (2ddcca7) was tested locally only.
evidence.security: This release contains one security fix: the empty LEMONADE_ADMIN_API_KEY bypass (5440e3e) that previously allowed unauthenticated access when the admin key was explicitly empty. The WebSocket credential transport fix (b1e53c4) was shipped in the previous bucket. No other security-relevant changes were observed.
